marks.gloss_en: ומה התם דגופין מוחלקין פטרי רבנן, הכא לא כל שכן -- the same a fortiori, for eating two nerves at once
ומה התם דגופין מוחלקין פטרי רבנן, הכא לא כל שכן? (kv_rabbanan_shnei_gidin)
[the tanna kamma is] the Rabbis, who dispute Sumakhos
תא שמע: אכל שני גידין משתי ירכות משתי בהמות -- סופג שמונים; at once with one warning, so the tanna kamma would be Sumakhos
מאי טעמא דרבי יהודה דאמר ארבעים ותו לא? -- sequentially with two warnings, why only forty?
ate two nerves from two thighs of two animals -- he incurs eighty
לעולם בזה אחר זה -- sequential; R' Yehuda's forty is because one nerve lacks an olive-bulk
דתניא: אכלו ואין בו כזית חייב; רבי יהודה אומר: עד שיהא בו כזית
and as for 'what is R' Yehuda's reason' -- [it is a case] where [one nerve] has no olive-bulk

'you shall not leave of it until morning, and what remains of it until morning you shall burn' -- the verse comes to give a positive command after the negative, to say that one is not flogged for it: the words of R' Yehuda
R' Yaakov: not for that reason, but because it is a negative command without an act
בידוע ששניהם שוחטין ביום אחד -- the groom and bride slaughter on the same day, so the interval does not help
R' Yehuda: when [must he inform]? when he has no interval; but if he has an interval he need not inform him
לפיכך -- since the butcher is compelled to slaughter on these occasions, if it dies it dies to the buyer
אינו כן, לפיכך -- on other days there is no such compulsion, therefore if it dies it dies to the seller
on these four occasions the butcher is made to slaughter against his will: even an ox worth a thousand dinars, and the buyer has only a dinar [in it], he is compelled to slaughter
on four occasions in the year one who sells an animal to his fellow must inform him: I sold its mother to slaughter, I sold its daughter to slaughter
נאמר כאן 'יום אחד' ונאמר במעשה בראשית 'יום אחד': as there the day follows the night, so of אותו ואת בנו -- against the יכול from the kodashim context
since the whole section speaks only of sacrificial animals
that it is proper conduct for the groom's house to exert itself more than the bride's house
it was taught: if he [the seller] did not inform him, he [the buyer] goes and slaughters and does not refrain
דאמר רבי יוחנן: דבר תורה מעות קונות, and pulling is only a decree lest he say 'your wheat burned in the loft'
R' Yochanan: by Torah law, money acquires
והא לא משך -- but the buyer never pulled the animal; how is it his loss?
והא לא משך! -- but he did not pull [the animal], so how can it die to the buyer?
אמר רב הונא אמר רב: כשמשך -- where he pulled it (= p_rav_keshemashach)
אי הכי, אימא סיפא: אבל בשאר ימות השנה אינו כן, לפיכך אם מת מת למוכר -- והא משך! -- if so, in the seifa too he pulled, yet it dies to the seller
Rav: [the mishna speaks] where he pulled [the animal]
לעולם שלא משך, וכגון שזיכה לו על ידי אחר -- on these occasions it is his benefit, and זכין לאדם שלא בפניו (= p_zikah_al_yedei_acher, p_zachin_leadam_shelo_befanav)
R' Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak: the mishna in fact speaks of one who did not pull, where [the seller] transferred it to him through another
R' Elazar in R' Yochanan's name: on these four occasions the Sages set their words upon Torah law (= p_heemidu_al_din_torah)
on these four occasions the Sages set their words upon Torah law
נאמר במעשה בראשית 'יום אחד' (Gen 1:5) ונאמר באותו ואת בנו 'יום אחד' (Lev 22:28): as there the day follows the night, so here
'one day' stated of [slaughtering] an animal and its offspring: the day follows the night
